newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says three foreign miners bid for La Oroya.
newsitem.headline: Peru says three foreign miners bid for La Oroya.

text.p: Three foreign mining firms formally started bidding for Peru's huge La Oroya metallurgic complex on Monday, state miner Centromin said.

Switzerland's Glencore International, Mexico's Industrias Penoles S.A. and the United States' Doe Run Co presented technical credentials, which, if approved, will allow them to make financial offers April 18.
Until last week, Spain's Asturiana de Zinc and Brazil's Paranapanema had also shown a strong interest in bidding but did not make formal presentations Monday, Centromin said.

Centromin has set a $70 million minimum bid price for the auction, whose terms oblige the winning firm to immediately inject the money offered at the sale into the complex as capital and then invest a further $120 million over the next five years.

La Oroya lies in the country's central Andes 12,300 feet (3,700 meters) above sea level and 120 miles (190 km) east of Lima. The complex of refineries and smelters La Oroya is Centromin's largest asset, processing 22 metals and their byproducts.
